chunks.text: # The Mathematics Pyramid, reconciled (MA, v2) Replaces both v1 versions: the four-layer MSC pyramid (K1–K4) and the five-object pyramid in the twelve volume. The object/method split of the twelve volume is kept as the primary partition, because every other pyramid uses it. The K-layers survive as the ORDER of Side A (dependency order) and as the grouping of Side C bridges. Every one of the 63 MSC2020 two-digit classes lands exactly once (checked by script). ## Governing thought Mathematics is exhausted by two sides of one pyramid: claims about

## 2. Governing thought Physics is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Its objects divide into five regimes: classical motion and fields, quantum systems, gravitation and the cosmos, matter in equilibrium, and matter out of equilibrium. ## 3. Key line Dimension: **the governing constants of the claim** (which of c, ħ, G and N set its scale). Logic inductive. Order: structural, from fewest constants to most, then the N axis. 1. Classical motion and fields 2. Quantum systems 3. Gravitation and the cosmos 4.

Matter in equilibrium 5. Matter out of equilibrium **Cube map.** This is an adaptation of the c–G–ħ cube of physical theories. It is not Bronstein's 1933 scheme, and the attribution of the cube's modern form is left open (UNVERIFIED). N is the author's axis. | Vertex | Theory | Home | |---|---|---| | none | Newtonian mechanics | PH.O.A1.1 | | c | special relativity; Maxwell electrodynamics | PH.O.A1.2–A1.3 | | ħ | non-relativistic quantum mechanics | PH.O.A2.1 | | c, ħ | quantum field theory | PH.O.A2.3 | |

G | Newtonian gravity | PH.O.A3.1 | | c, G | general relativity | PH.O.A3.2 | | G, ħ | no established theory | REFUSED as a cell. Such claims go to PH.O.A3.5, OPEN | | c, G, ħ | quantum gravity | PH.O.A3.5, OPEN | | N, equilibrium | thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, condensed matter | PH.O.A4 | | N, driven or relaxing | transport, fluids, plasma, radiation in matter, nonlinear dynamics | PH.O.A5 | **MECE test.** Exclusive: each claim is placed by the largest set of constants its derivation

needs. Exhaustive: every vertex of the cube, and both states of the N axis, has a home or a stated refusal. **CONTESTED.** Newtonian gravity is placed in A3, not A1, so all gravitation shares one home. The alternative files it in A1 by the "no c, no ħ" rule. ## 4. Face O — Objects ### PH.O.A1 Classical motion and fields **SCQA.** Bodies and fields move by deterministic laws when ħ and G are negligible. Classical physics remains the working physics of engineering and much of astronomy. Which laws are

claimed, and within what limits? The limits are speeds below c for mechanics, and actions much larger than ħ throughout. **Key line.** Particle mechanics, classical fields, special relativity, symmetry and conservation, continua. - **PH.O.A1.1 Particle mechanics.** Newton's laws hold in inertial frames for speeds much below c. - PH.O.A1.1.1 Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics are equivalent where the Legendre transform is regular. - PH.O.A1.1.2 Liouville's theorem: Hamiltonian flow preserves phase-space volume. The theorem is MA.O.A4; its physical use is here. - PH.O.A1.1.3 Rigid-body motion, oscillators and small vibrations. - **PH.O.A1.2 Classical

fields.** Maxwell's equations govern electromagnetic fields in vacuum, and in linear media given constitutive relations. - PH.O.A1.2.1 Electrostatics and magnetostatics, including the quasistatic circuit laws (Kirchhoff) as the limit of slow change. - PH.O.A1.2.2 Electromagnetic waves; c is the propagation speed in vacuum. - PH.O.A1.2.3 Classical optics: geometric optics in the short-wavelength limit; diffraction and interference. - **PH.O.A1.3 Special relativity.** The laws take the same form in all inertial frames, and c is frame-invariant. - PH.O.A1.3.1 Lorentz transformations; time dilation; length contraction. - PH.O.A1.3.2 Mass–energy equivalence, E = mc² for

a body at rest. - **PH.O.A1.4 Symmetry and conservation.** Noether: each continuous symmetry of a local action yields a conserved current. The theorem is MA (uses MA.O.A4); the physical conservation law is PH. - PH.O.A1.4.1 Energy, momentum and angular momentum from time, space and rotation symmetry. - PH.O.A1.4.2 Charge conservation from the gauge symmetry of electrodynamics. - **PH.O.A1.5 Continuum mechanics.** Solids and fluids are treated as continua where the medium is smooth on the scale of interest. Cauchy stress gives traction t = σᵀn. - PH.O.A1.5.1 Linear elasticity: Hooke's law

for small strain in a linear elastic solid. - PH.O.A1.5.2 Constitutive laws close the balance equations. The artefact meeting a specification is EN. ### PH.O.A2 Quantum systems **SCQA.** When action is comparable to ħ, states superpose and measurement yields statistics, not trajectories. Quantum theory is the most precisely tested theory in physics, yet its interpretation is disputed. What is claimed, and what is left to philosophy? **Key line.** States and dynamics, non-locality, fields and particles, atoms and light, interpretation. - **PH.O.A2.1 States and dynamics.** A closed system's state evolves unitarily

by the Schrödinger equation. The Born rule gives outcome probabilities. - PH.O.A2.1.1 The uncertainty relation σ_x σ_p ≥ ħ/2 holds for any state (the theorem is MA.O.A2, as operator algebra). - PH.O.A2.1.2 Decoherence: interaction with an environment suppresses interference in a preferred basis. It does not by itself select a single outcome. - PH.O.A2.1.3 Tunnelling and bound states. - **PH.O.A2.2 Non-locality.** Bell: any local hidden-variable theory with measurement independence obeys the CHSH bound S ≤ 2. Quantum mechanics reaches 2√2 (the Tsirelson bound). Loophole-free violations were reported in 2015 (Delft,

Vienna, NIST). - PH.O.A2.2.1 Entanglement as a resource: teleportation, quantum key distribution. Deployed protocols are CS.O.A5. - PH.O.A2.2.2 No-signalling: entanglement cannot transmit information faster than light. - **PH.O.A2.3 Quantum fields and particles.** The Standard Model describes three of the four known interactions, with gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1). - PH.O.A2.3.1 Spin–statistics and CPT hold for local, Lorentz-invariant quantum field theories with energy bounded below. - PH.O.A2.3.2 The Higgs boson was observed in 2012 (ATLAS and CMS). - PH.O.A2.3.3 Neutrino oscillation implies non-zero neutrino masses. The mass ordering is OPEN. - PH.O.A2.3.5 Nuclear

structure and decay: half-lives are measured constants (W4), e.g. the ¹⁴C half-life of 5,730 ± 40 years. Radiometric ages built on them are EA. - PH.O.A2.3.4 Renormalisation: physics at low energy is insensitive to most details at high energy, for renormalisable theories and effective field theories. - **PH.O.A2.4 Atomic, molecular and optical physics.** Atomic level structure, spectra, and the interaction of light with atoms. The chemical bond is CH; PH owns the level structure. - PH.O.A2.4.1 Lasers: stimulated emission in a medium with population inversion. - PH.O.A2.4.2 Laser cooling and

Bose–Einstein condensation of dilute gases (first achieved 1995). - PH.O.A2.4.3 Atomic clocks and precision measurement. The SI second has been defined by the caesium-133 hyperfine transition since 1967. - **PH.O.A2.5 Interpretation of quantum mechanics.** CONTESTED placement. The empirical content stays here. Copenhagen, many-worlds, pilot-wave and collapse theories, as arguments, are PL. ### PH.O.A3 Gravitation and the cosmos **SCQA.** Where G matters, gravity shapes motion, and at high mass or speed it shapes spacetime itself. The cosmos is the only laboratory at the largest scales. What is claimed, and what is

still open? **Key line.** Newtonian gravity, general relativity, astrophysics, cosmology, quantum gravity. - **PH.O.A3.1 Newtonian gravity.** The inverse-square attraction is valid for weak fields and speeds much below c. - PH.O.A3.1.1 Kepler's laws follow for two point masses. - PH.O.A3.1.2 Celestial mechanics: perturbation theory for many bodies. The n-body problem's mathematics is MA.O.A4. - **PH.O.A3.2 General relativity.** Einstein's field equations relate spacetime curvature to stress-energy. The equivalence principle holds locally. - PH.O.A3.2.1 Classical tests: Mercury's perihelion, light deflection, gravitational redshift. - PH.O.A3.2.2 Black holes: the Schwarzschild and Kerr solutions. Singularity

theorems (Penrose, Hawking) assume energy conditions and trapped surfaces (uses MA.O.A3). - PH.O.A3.2.3 Gravitational waves: first detected 14 September 2015, announced February 2016 (LIGO). - **PH.O.A3.3 Astrophysics.** Stars, compact objects, galaxies. - PH.O.A3.3.1 Stellar structure and nucleosynthesis. - PH.O.A3.3.2 The Chandrasekhar limit: about 1.4 solar masses for a non-rotating white dwarf supported by electron degeneracy pressure. - PH.O.A3.3.3 Neutron stars, pulsars, accretion. - **PH.O.A3.4 Cosmology.** ΛCDM fits the expansion history, the cosmic microwave background and large-scale structure. - PH.O.A3.4.1 Hubble–Lemaître expansion. The "Hubble tension" between early- and late-universe measurements is

OPEN. - PH.O.A3.4.2 The CMB, discovered 1965. - PH.O.A3.4.3 Dark matter and dark energy: inferred from gravity; their identities are OPEN. - PH.O.A3.4.4 Inflation: a CONTESTED programme with supporting but not decisive evidence. - **PH.O.A3.5 Quantum gravity.** OPEN. - PH.O.A3.5.1 Bekenstein–Hawking entropy S = k_B c³ A / (4Għ) for a black hole of horizon area A. (The v1 omission of k_B is fixed.) - PH.O.A3.5.2 Hawking radiation: a semiclassical prediction (quantum fields on a curved background), not yet observed for astrophysical black holes. - PH.O.A3.5.3 Programmes: string theory, loop

quantum gravity, asymptotic safety. All lack decisive empirical tests. ### PH.O.A4 Matter in equilibrium **SCQA.** Many bodies at equilibrium show laws that no single body shows: temperature, phases, rigidity. Equilibrium is an idealisation, but a very good one for most matter at rest. What is claimed? **Key line.** Thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, phase transitions, condensed states. - **PH.O.A4.1 Thermodynamics.** - PH.O.A4.1.1 First law: the change in internal energy of a closed system equals heat in minus work out (sign convention stated). - PH.O.A4.1.2 Second law: the entropy of an isolated system

does not decrease. Carnot efficiency 1 − T_c/T_h bounds any engine between two reservoirs. - PH.O.A4.1.3 Third law: entropy approaches a constant as T → 0, for systems with a non-degenerate ground state. - **PH.O.A4.2 Statistical mechanics.** Ensembles derive thermodynamics from microstates. The microcanonical ensemble assumes equilibrium and equal a priori probability. - PH.O.A4.2.1 Boltzmann entropy S = k_B ln W. - PH.O.A4.2.2 Quantum statistics: Fermi–Dirac and Bose–Einstein distributions for indistinguishable particles. - PH.O.A4.2.3 Ergodic hypothesis: CONTESTED as a justification. The ergodic theorems are MA.O.A4. - **PH.O.A4.3 Phase transitions.** -

PH.O.A4.3.1 Clapeyron equation: dP/dT = L/(T Δv) on a coexistence line. - PH.O.A4.3.2 Clausius–Clapeyron: d ln P/dT = L/(RT²). It adds an ideal vapour, negligible condensed-phase volume and constant L. (The v1 mislabel is fixed.) - PH.O.A4.3.3 Critical phenomena and universality: systems with the same dimension, symmetry and interaction range share critical exponents. Renormalisation-group explanation (Wilson). - PH.O.A4.3.4 Mermin–Wagner: no spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at T > 0 in d ≤ 2 with short-range interactions. - **PH.O.A4.4 Condensed states.** Band structure, superconductivity, magnetism, topological phases, defects. - PH.O.A4.4.1

Quasiparticles: an excitation with decay rate Γ = 1/τ is well defined when ħΓ is much less than its energy. (The v1 lifetime–rate confusion is fixed.) - PH.O.A4.4.2 BCS theory of conventional superconductivity: electron pairing mediated by phonons, for weak coupling. High-temperature superconductivity mechanisms are OPEN. - PH.O.A4.4.3 Semiconductors and device physics: drift–diffusion transport in the low-injection regime. - PH.O.A4.4.4 Dislocations as the mechanism of plastic flow in crystals. - PH.O.A4.4.5 Topological phases: quantum Hall effects (integer 1980, fractional 1982). ### PH.O.A5 Matter out of equilibrium **SCQA.** v1 had no

home for driven or relaxing matter, yet most of nature is out of equilibrium. Which laws hold away from equilibrium, and how far away? **Key line.** Transport, fluids, plasmas, radiation and matter, nonlinear dynamics. - **PH.O.A5.1 Transport near equilibrium.** - PH.O.A5.1.1 Linear response; the fluctuation–dissipation theorem for systems near equilibrium. - PH.O.A5.1.2 Onsager reciprocity: assumes microscopic reversibility, with the magnetic field reversed when one is present. - PH.O.A5.1.3 Diffusion, conduction, viscosity as transport coefficients; Boltzmann transport equation for dilute gases. - **PH.O.A5.2 Fluids.** Navier–Stokes governs Newtonian fluids. Global smoothness in

three dimensions is OPEN and owned by MA.O.A4. - PH.O.A5.2.1 Turbulence: Kolmogorov's 1941 scaling for homogeneous isotropic turbulence at high Reynolds number. A full theory is OPEN. - PH.O.A5.2.2 Dimensionless groups (Reynolds, Mach) set the regime. - **PH.O.A5.3 Plasmas.** Quasi-neutral ionised matter, collective behaviour on scales larger than the Debye length. - PH.O.A5.3.1 Magnetohydrodynamics, valid where collisions keep a fluid description. - PH.O.A5.3.2 Fusion plasmas: Lawson criterion for net energy gain, given confinement time and density at a stated temperature. - **PH.O.A5.4 Radiation and matter.** - PH.O.A5.4.1 Planck's law for

blackbody radiation in thermal equilibrium; Stefan–Boltzmann law as its integral. - PH.O.A5.4.2 Radiative transfer through absorbing and emitting media. - PH.O.A5.4.3 Interaction of ionising radiation with matter (stopping, attenuation). Nuclear decay itself, with its half-lives, moved to PH.O.A2.3.5 after the pilot (claim 38). - **PH.O.A5.5 Nonlinear dynamics and complex systems.** Sensitive dependence on initial conditions; pattern formation; active matter. Theorems are MA.O.A4; the physical system is here. - PH.O.A5.5.1 Non-equilibrium fluctuation theorems (Jarzynski, Crooks) for systems driven from an initial equilibrium.

## 2. Governing thought Chemistry is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Its objects divide into five questions about a substance: composition and identity, structure and bonding, equilibrium and energy, rates and mechanisms, and synthesis and analysis. ## 3. Key line Dimension: **the question asked of a substance.** Logic inductive. Order: structural, from what a substance is to how it is made or found. 1. Composition and identity 2. Structure and bonding 3. Equilibrium and energy 4. Rates and mechanisms 5. Synthesis and analysis

**MECE test.** "The yield of this esterification at 60 °C is 85%" is A5 (a claim about making). "Its rate constant at 60 °C is k" is A4. "Its equilibrium constant is K" is A3. The same reaction gets three sentences, each with one home. ## 4. Face O — Objects ### CH.O.A1 Composition and identity **SCQA.** Before any other claim, a substance must be named and its make-up fixed. Identity rests partly on convention (names, identifiers) and partly on measurement (composition). What is it? **Key line.** Elements, compounds and

stoichiometry, mixtures and solutions, nomenclature and identifiers, isotopes. - **CH.O.A1.1 Elements and the periodic table.** 118 elements are named and confirmed by IUPAC; the last four names were approved in 2016. Periodicity follows from electron configuration (uses PH.O.A2.1). - CH.O.A1.1.1 Atomic weights are published by IUPAC (CIAAW), some as intervals reflecting natural variation. - **CH.O.A1.2 Compounds and stoichiometry.** The law of definite proportions holds for daltonide compounds. Berthollide (non-stoichiometric) solids, such as wüstite Fe₁₋ₓO, are the stated exception. - CH.O.A1.2.1 The mole: since 2019 defined by fixing the Avogadro constant

at 6.022 140 76 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. - **CH.O.A1.3 Mixtures and solutions.** Composition is stated by mole fraction, molality or concentration. - CH.O.A1.3.1 Raoult's law holds for ideal solutions. Henry's law holds for dilute solutes. - CH.O.A1.3.2 Colligative properties depend on solute particle number, for dilute ideal solutions. - **CH.O.A1.4 Nomenclature and identifiers.** IUPAC names, CAS registry numbers and InChI. Warrant W12. - **CH.O.A1.5 Isotopes and isotopic composition.** Isotope ratios as identity and tracer. The nuclear structure is PH; radiometric ages are EA. ### CH.O.A2 Structure and bonding **SCQA.** A

substance's properties follow from how its atoms are arranged and held together. Bonding models range from exact quantum chemistry to heuristic rules. What is claimed about structure, and by which model? **Key line.** The chemical bond, molecular shape, solid-state and coordination structure, intermolecular forces. - **CH.O.A2.1 The chemical bond.** Covalent, ionic and metallic bonding. The quantum-chemical description uses the Born–Oppenheimer approximation: nuclei treated as fixed relative to electrons. - CH.O.A2.1.1 Molecular orbital theory and valence bond theory as models. - CH.O.A2.1.2 Electronegativity (Pauling scale) as a derived, model-dependent quantity. -

**CH.O.A2.2 Molecular shape and stereochemistry.** Chirality, isomerism, conformational analysis. VSEPR is listed as a heuristic, not a law. - CH.O.A2.2.1 Enantiomers have identical scalar properties in an achiral environment. They differ in chiral environments, including living systems (BI, MD). - **CH.O.A2.3 Solid-state and coordination structure.** Crystal structures; ligand field theory for transition-metal complexes. - CH.O.A2.3.1 Polymorphism: one compound, several crystal forms with different properties. - **CH.O.A2.4 Intermolecular forces.** Hydrogen bonding, dipole forces, dispersion; their effect on phase and solubility. ### CH.O.A3 Equilibrium and energy **SCQA.** Thermodynamics decides which way a

reaction runs and how far. It says nothing about speed. What is claimed about the direction and extent of change? **Key line.** Thermochemistry, chemical equilibrium, electrochemistry, acids and bases, solution thermodynamics. - **CH.O.A3.1 Thermochemistry.** Hess's law: the enthalpy change is path-independent because enthalpy is a state function. Enthalpies of reaction enter energy balances in EN. - **CH.O.A3.2 Chemical equilibrium.** ΔG° = −RT ln K at constant temperature and pressure. Le Chatelier's principle is listed as a heuristic for small perturbations. - CH.O.A3.2.1 The van 't Hoff equation gives the temperature

dependence of K, assuming ΔH° constant over the range. - **CH.O.A3.3 Electrochemistry.** The Nernst equation E = E° − (RT/nF) ln Q, using activities, for a cell at equilibrium (no current). It gives ion equilibrium potentials used in BI and MS. - CH.O.A3.3.1 Batteries and corrosion as applications. Device performance is EN. - **CH.O.A3.4 Acids and bases.** Brønsted–Lowry and Lewis definitions. pKa is stated in a named solvent and at a temperature. - **CH.O.A3.5 Free energy in coupled reactions.** A favourable reaction can drive an unfavourable one when they share

an intermediate. ATP coupling in cells is the BI application. ### CH.O.A4 Rates and mechanisms **SCQA.** Thermodynamics says whether; kinetics says how fast and by what path. Mechanisms are inferred, never observed whole. What is claimed about speed and pathway? **Key line.** Rate laws, temperature dependence, mechanisms, catalysis, photochemistry. - **CH.O.A4.1 Rate laws.** Reaction order is determined by experiment, not by the balanced equation, except for elementary steps. - **CH.O.A4.2 Temperature dependence.** Arrhenius k = A exp(−Ea/RT) is empirical over a stated temperature range. Eyring transition-state theory assumes quasi-equilibrium with

the activated complex. - **CH.O.A4.3 Mechanisms.** Sequences of elementary steps. The steady-state and rate-determining-step approximations hold when one step is much slower than the rest. - CH.O.A4.3.1 Kinetic isotope effects as mechanistic evidence. - **CH.O.A4.4 Catalysis.** A catalyst changes the rate without changing K. Heterogeneous, homogeneous and enzyme catalysis. Michaelis–Menten kinetics assume a steady-state enzyme–substrate complex and substrate in excess. The enzyme's role in life is BI. - **CH.O.A4.5 Photochemistry.** Reactions initiated by light; quantum yield. The level structure is PH.O.A2.4. ### CH.O.A5 Synthesis and analysis **SCQA.** Chemistry makes substances

and finds out what a sample contains. Both are practical claims with stated conditions. What was made, how, and how do we know what is there? **Key line.** Synthesis, separation and purification, analytical measurement, materials and polymers, green chemistry. - **CH.O.A5.1 Synthesis.** Named reactions; retrosynthetic analysis (Corey); yields under stated conditions. - CH.O.A5.1.1 Protecting groups and selectivity. - **CH.O.A5.2 Separation and purification.** Distillation, chromatography, crystallisation. - **CH.O.A5.3 Analytical measurement.** Spectroscopy (NMR, IR, UV-vis), mass spectrometry, titration. Every value carries an uncertainty and a detection limit. - CH.O.A5.3.1 The Beer–Lambert law

holds for dilute solutions and monochromatic light, without scattering. - **CH.O.A5.4 Materials and polymers.** Composition–property relations for designed substances. Performance against a specification is EN. - **CH.O.A5.5 Green chemistry.** Atom economy and waste metrics. The environmental impact claim is EV.

## 2. Governing thought Biology is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Every biological claim is about one of five levels or processes: Heritable information · Cell · Organism · Descent · Ecological interaction. ## 3. Key line - Logic: inductive. - Plural noun: levels or processes of living organisation. - Dimension: the level or process the claim is about. - Order: structural, from the copied sequence to the interacting community. Members (5): 1. Heritable information 2. Cell 3. Organism 4. Descent 5. Ecological

interaction Assignment note on the dimension. Heritable information and Descent are processes, not sizes. The dimension is therefore "level or process", not "unit, small to large" (audit error 5). Population has one home per question: allele-frequency change goes to Descent (BI.O.A4); numbers, rates and growth go to Ecological interaction (BI.O.A5). ## 4. Face O — Objects ### BI.O.A1 Heritable information Situation. Living things copy sequence and pass it on. Complication. The chemistry of the nucleotide is also claimed by chemistry, and the central dogma is often misstated as a ban.

Question. Which claims about heredity does biology own? Answer. Biology owns what is copied, how it is read, how it is passed on and how it varies. Chemistry owns the bond energetics (uses CH.O.A3). Key line (inductive; plural noun: heredity processes; dimension: what happens to the sequence; order: life cycle of a sequence). Members (4): Replication · Expression and regulation · Transmission · Variation. - BI.O.A1.1 Replication. Template copying of DNA, or RNA in some viruses, with stated fidelity. Copying fidelity as heredity is owned here. The template chemistry and

base-pair energetics are owned by CH.O.A3 (uses CH.O.A3). - BI.O.A1.2 Expression and regulation. The genetic code maps codons to amino acids. It is a mapping, nearly universal, with known variant codes. It is owned here; CH.O.A3 cites it. Crick's central dogma (1970) states that sequence information, once in protein, cannot transfer back to nucleic acid or to other protein. Reverse transcription (RNA to DNA) is a "special transfer" allowed by it. The slogan DNA → RNA → protein is a heuristic (BI.M.H). Regulation covers transcription factors, chromatin state and noncoding

RNA. Epigenetic marks can persist across mitotic divisions. Transgenerational epigenetic inheritance is a separate, narrower claim and is OPEN in many taxa. - BI.O.A1.3 Transmission. Mendel's laws: segregation holds for a diploid locus under regular meiosis; independent assortment holds only for loci that are unlinked. Linkage is the exception that maps chromosomes. Horizontal gene transfer moves sequence between lineages and breaks a strictly branching tree. Plasmids are its common vehicle in prokaryotes. - BI.O.A1.4 Variation. Mutation is a change in sequence: point, indel, copy-number or chromosomal. Its fitness effect is

a later claim (BI.O.A4), not part of the definition. Recombination generates new allele combinations. The gene has two definitions, molecular (transcribed region) and classical (unit of inheritance); a sentence must say which. Named objects: allele, genotype, phenotype, locus, codon, plasmid, recombination, horizontal transfer, epigenetic mark. ### BI.O.A2 Cell Situation. The cell is the smallest unit that is alive. Complication. Viruses replicate but are not cells, and v1 filed them twice. Membranes and ATP were also filed in chemistry. Question. Which claims about the cell does biology own? Answer. Biology owns

the cell plan, its membrane and excitability, its metabolism as organised chemistry, its division, and the acellular replicators that depend on it. Key line (inductive; plural noun: cell functions; dimension: what part of cell life the claim is about; order: structure, then flux, then reproduction, then dependants). Members (5): Cell plans and origin · Membrane, excitability and signalling · Metabolism · Cycle and division · Acellular replicators. - BI.O.A2.1 Cell plans and origin. Cell theory: organisms are cells or assemblages of cells, and cells arise from cells. It is a

historical generalisation with one stated exception class: the origin of life. Prokaryotic plans (bacteria, archaea) lack a nucleus. Eukaryotic plans have a nucleus and membrane-bounded organelles. Endosymbiosis explains mitochondria and plastids. Origin of life is an OPEN programme; it uses CH.O.A3 and EA.O.A3. - BI.O.A2.2 Membrane, excitability and signalling. A lipid bilayer sets an inside; transport is passive or pumped. The resting membrane potential is owned here. The Nernst equation that gives each ion's equilibrium potential is owned by chemistry (uses CH.O.A3.3). The action potential is owned here as an

excitable-membrane claim. CONTESTED: alternative home MS.O.A2. Signalling covers receptor, second messenger and response. Specificity is binding, not a new force. - BI.O.A2.3 Metabolism. Pathways capture and spend energy. ATP and proton-motive force as cell currency are owned here. ATP coupling as free energy (ΔG) is owned by CH.O.A3 (uses CH.O.A3). Enzyme kinetics, including Michaelis–Menten, is owned by CH.O.A4.2. Michaelis–Menten holds under a quasi-steady-state complex, substrate in excess of enzyme, and no product inhibition (uses CH.O.A4.2). Photosynthesis and aerobic respiration are the two dominant planetary routes. Chemosynthesis (chemolithotrophy) and fermentation are

other major routes. - BI.O.A2.4 Cycle and division. Replication, segregation and division, with checkpoints. Mitosis preserves ploidy. Meiosis halves ploidy and recombines homologues. - BI.O.A2.5 Acellular replicators. Viruses, viroids and similar replicators reproduce only inside a host cell. The Baltimore scheme classifies viruses into seven classes by genome type and route to mRNA. Quasispecies theory describes mutant swarms under high mutation rate; its fit to real viral populations is CONTESTED. Virology as a named group is in the catalog register (BI.B.K). Named objects: cell theory, prokaryote, eukaryote, endosymbiosis, membrane potential,

action potential, ATP, proton-motive force, mitosis, meiosis, Baltimore class. ### BI.O.A3 Organism Situation. One individual integrates cells into a working body. Complication. Medicine restates normal physiology, mind claims behaviour, and agriculture and veterinary science had no home. Question. Which claims about the individual organism does biology own? Answer. Biology owns normal function, development, defence, behaviour of non-human animals, and the organism in production with its disorders. Human disorder is MD. Key line (inductive; plural noun: organismal functions; dimension: what the individual must do or undergo; order: maintain, build, defend, act,

be used). Members (5): Homeostasis and exchange · Development and life history · Immune defence · Behaviour · Production and animal health. - BI.O.A3.1 Homeostasis and exchange. Regulated variables are held in a range by negative feedback; not every internal value is constant. Exchange of gas, water, solute and heat is constrained by surface-to-volume ratio. Circulation and branching relieve that constraint. Chronobiology (circadian and other clocks) is a homeostatic-control claim and lives here. Normal human physiology is owned here; MD.O.A1 cites it. - BI.O.A3.2 Development and life history. Development turns

one cell into a patterned body. Differentiation is change in gene expression under position and history. Morphogen gradients and induction are mechanisms, not universal laws. A stem cell can self-renew and produce differentiated daughters; potency is a measured range. Life history covers growth, reproduction and ageing, with trade-offs as the claim. Evo-devo lives here and cites BI.O.A4. - BI.O.A3.3 Immune defence. Innate and adaptive recognition, and self versus non-self as a functional distinction with known failures. The antibody as a molecule is CH.O.A3; the system is organismal. Normal immune function

is owned here; human immune disorder is MD.O.A1.1. - BI.O.A3.4 Behaviour. Action selected by sensory input and internal state in non-human animals. Ethology and behavioural ecology of individuals live here. Neural circuits and systems are owned by MS.O.A2. Human behaviour is owned by MS.O.A1. - BI.O.A3.5 Production and animal health. The organism kept or grown for use: crop, livestock, aquaculture and forestry organisms. Husbandry claims state the conditions, the population and the measure; no universal yield is owned. substance and its residue in human food are owned by MD.O.A4.1 (uses MD.O.A4.1, MD.O.A4.4). The food molecule is CH; a food standard is W12. Named objects: homeostasis, negative feedback, morphogen, stem cell, potency, circadian clock, innate immunity, adaptive immunity, ethogram, yield, animal disease. ### BI.O.A4 Descent Situation. Lineages change across generations. Complication. Population genetics, quantitative genetics and phylogeny were split across two v1 bridges. Hardy–Weinberg and heritability lacked hypotheses or a cell. Question. Which claims

about change across generations does biology own? Answer. Biology owns the processes that change allele frequencies, the genetics of continuous traits, the splitting of lineages, the pattern of relationship and the pattern above the species. Key line (inductive; plural noun: descent claims; dimension: the resolution of the change; order: within population to above species). Members (5): Population-genetic processes · Quantitative genetics · Speciation · Phylogenetic pattern · Macroevolution. - BI.O.A4.1 Population-genetic processes. Natural selection: heritable variation that affects reproductive success changes allele frequencies. Drift is stronger in small effective populations.

Hardy–Weinberg principle: with no selection, mutation, migration or drift (very large population), and random mating at an autosomal locus with discrete generations, allele frequencies stay constant. Under the same conditions genotype frequencies reach p², 2pq, q² after one generation. Nonrandom mating alone changes genotype frequencies, not allele frequencies. Hardy–Weinberg is a null model, not a mechanism. The Price equation partitions change in a mean trait into selection and transmission terms; it is an identity given defined fitness and trait values. Hamilton's rule (rB > C) holds under its derivation's assumptions,

typically weak selection and additive fitness effects; its generality is CONTESTED. An evolutionarily stable strategy is the MA solution concept applied to fitness payoffs (uses MA.B.C4). Fitness is reproductive success in a stated environment. - BI.O.A4.2 Quantitative genetics. Broad-sense heritability H² = V_G/V_P. Narrow-sense heritability h² = V_A/V_P. Both are variance ratios in a stated population and environment, not individual destinies. The breeder's equation R = h²S holds for a trait under truncation-like selection, with additive effects and no genotype–environment covariance. Human heritability estimates are owned here; MS.O.A3 cites them.

- BI.O.A4.3 Speciation. Lineages cease to exchange genes. Allopatric, parapatric and sympatric routes differ in geography; none is required. Species concepts (biological, phylogenetic, morphological) are naming practice in BI.M.5. - BI.O.A4.4 Phylogenetic pattern. A phylogeny is a hypothesis of relationship. A clade is a common ancestor and all its descendants. Rank (family, order) is a convention (W12). Horizontal transfer and incomplete lineage sorting make gene trees differ from species trees. - BI.O.A4.5 Macroevolution. Pattern above the species, read from phylogeny and fossils. It needs no separate mechanism, though rates and

constraints differ. The organism biology of fossils is owned here; occurrence in a stratum is EA.O.A3. Mass-extinction tempo is a pattern claim shared by citation with EA.O.A3. Named objects: natural selection, drift, Hardy–Weinberg, Price equation, Hamilton's rule, ESS, heritability, breeder's equation, clade, species tree, gene tree. ### BI.O.A5 Ecological interaction Situation. Organisms act on each other and on matter and energy. Complication. Population growth was double-filed with descent; Lotka–Volterra was filed as a method. own? Answer. Biology owns non-human population dynamics, pairwise interactions, community structure, ecosystem flux and the distribution of life. Key line (inductive; plural noun: interaction claims; dimension: the number of parties and the currency; order: one population to the biosphere). Members (5): Population dynamics · Interactions · Community · Ecosystem flux · Biogeography. - BI.O.A5.1 Population dynamics. Exponential growth dN/dt = rN holds for constant per-capita rate r with unlimited resources and no structure. Logistic growth dN/dt = rN(1 − N/K) adds a fixed carrying capacity K and linear density dependence.

K holds only in a stated setting. Human demography is owned by MS.O.A5. - BI.O.A5.2 Interactions. Classified by the sign of the effect on each party: competition (−/−), predation and parasitism (+/−), mutualism (+/+), commensalism (+/0), amensalism (−/0), and neutralism (0/0) as the null. The Lotka–Volterra predator–prey equations assume a well-mixed system, exponential prey growth without predators, and linear functional responses. The equation is owned here; its simulation is BI.M.4. - BI.O.A5.3 Community. Who co-occurs, and the structure of the interaction web. Diversity is a count or a named index;

say which. Niche is the set of conditions and resources under which a population persists, fundamental versus realised. The host-associated microbiome is a community claim here, citing BI.O.A3 for host function. - BI.O.A5.4 Ecosystem flux. Energy flow and matter cycling through a community plus the abiotic pool. Trophic transfer efficiency measured across ecosystems runs about 5–20 percent (Pauly and Christensen 1995). The 10 percent rule is a heuristic (BI.M.H). Biological carbon and nitrogen fluxes are owned here. CONTESTED: AGU files them in Biogeosciences; alternative home EA.O.A4.3. Water balance is EA.O.A4.2.

- BI.O.A5.5 Biogeography. The spatial distribution of life, set by dispersal, barrier, climate and history. Endemism and disjunction are patterns needing a historical explanation. CONTESTED: alternative EA.O.A4 for the map pattern alone. Island biogeography theory (MacArthur–Wilson) holds under a balance of immigration and extinction depending on isolation and area; its equilibrium assumption is CONTESTED. Named objects: carrying capacity, Lotka–Volterra, niche, diversity index, food web, trophic efficiency, microbiome, endemism, island biogeography.

Every Earth claim is about one of five questions: Materials · Internal motion · Deep time · Surface and fluid envelopes · Human spatial organization. ## 3. Key line - Logic: inductive. - Plural noun: questions about the Earth. - Dimension: what the claim is about. - Order: structural, from rock to settlement. Members (5): 1. Materials 2. 5. Human spatial organization Change from v1. "Surface pattern" becomes "Surface and fluid envelopes". O — Objects ### EA.O.A1 Materials Situation. Minerals, rocks, crustal fluids and soil parent material make up the solid Earth. Complication. Chemistry claims the bond and speciation; v1 defined a mineral too narrowly and gave metamorphic facies a single P–T point. Question. Which claims about Earth materials does EA own? Answer. EA owns identity, assemblage, origin class and distribution of materials in Earth reservoirs. Speciation chemistry is CH. Key line (inductive; plural noun: material classes; dimension: the origin or state of the material; order: crystal to fluid). Members (5): Minerals

· Igneous rocks · Sedimentary rocks · Metamorphic rocks · Crustal fluids and element distribution. - EA.O.A1.1 Minerals. IMA definition: a mineral is an element or compound, normally crystalline, formed by geological processes (Nickel 1995). Its composition is definite but not necessarily fixed, allowing solid solution. Silicates dominate the crust. Identification is by habit, cleavage, hardness, optics, XRD and microprobe. Names follow IMA (W12). - EA.O.A1.2 Igneous rocks. Formed from melt. Texture records cooling rate. Bowen's reaction series is the idealised crystallisation order of a basaltic melt cooling slowly with

equilibrium reaction. Few magmas complete it. Classification follows IUGS (W12). - EA.O.A1.3 Sedimentary rocks. Formed by deposition and lithification. Grain size, sorting and composition are the descriptors. A sedimentary structure (cross-bed, ripple, graded bed) is evidence of the depositing process. Sedimentology is the A1 process claim; the sequence is EA.O.A3. - EA.O.A1.4 Metamorphic rocks. Formed by solid-state change. A metamorphic facies (Eskola 1920) is a set of mineral assemblages formed over a stated range of pressure and temperature. Foliation records directed stress. The rock cycle is a path among A1.2–A1.4,

not a clock. - EA.O.A1.5 Crustal fluids and element distribution. Groundwater, brines, hydrothermal fluids and melts in the crust. Element distribution in Earth reservoirs (geochemistry as distribution) is owned here. Speciation and reaction in a natural matrix is CH (uses CH, environmental chemistry cell). Soil parent material is here; the soil body is EA.O.A4.4. Named objects: mineral, solid solution, Bowen's series, facies, foliation, cross-bed, rock cycle, ore deposit (application instance), hydrothermal fluid. ### EA.O.A2 Internal motion Situation. Heat and gravity drive motion in the interior and lithosphere. Complication. v1 said

"magnitude is energy", stated isostasy imprecisely, and left the geodynamo and geodesy unplaced. Question. Which claims about how the Earth moves inside does EA own? Answer. EA owns plate kinematics, deformation, interior structure and fields, isostatic support, and magmatism. Wave and elasticity laws are PH. Key line (inductive; plural noun: motion claims; dimension: what moves and at what depth; order: surface plates to deep interior and back to melt). Members (5): Plate kinematics · Deformation · Interior structure and fields · Isostasy and flexure · Magmatism. - EA.O.A2.1 Plate kinematics.

The lithosphere is divided into plates that move relative to one another. Boundaries are divergent, convergent or transform. Evidence: continental fit, rock and fossil correlation, seafloor magnetic anomalies, seismicity, and geodetic motion. Euler-pole description of plate motion holds for rigid plates on a sphere. - EA.O.A2.2 Deformation. Stress and strain in rock. Brittle faulting dominates near the surface; ductile flow dominates at depth. A fold is geometry; a fault is a fracture with offset. Earthquake size: magnitude is a logarithmic measure. Moment magnitude Mw derives from seismic moment M₀ =

μAD (rigidity, rupture area, mean slip). Radiated energy rises about 32 times per unit magnitude. Intensity is felt effect (USGS, cited in audit). - EA.O.A2.3 Interior structure and fields. Seismology infers layering from travel times. S waves do not pass through the outer core, which is evidence it is liquid. The geodynamo (the field generated in the liquid outer core) is owned here as an Earth-state claim. The MHD equations used are PH. Geodesy as a claim — figure of the Earth, gravity field — is owned here. - EA.O.A2.4

Isostasy and flexure. The lithosphere is in buoyant equilibrium on the asthenosphere. Airy compensation uses crustal roots; Pratt compensation uses lateral density change. Many ranges are partly supported by flexure of an elastic plate. Glacial isostatic adjustment is the observable rebound after ice load. - EA.O.A2.5 Magmatism. Melt generation at ridges (decompression), subduction zones (flux melting) and hotspots. A hotspot track is evidence of plate motion over a source, interpreted, not seen. Volcanic eruption as a hazard event enters EA.O.A5.5. Named objects: plate, Euler pole, transform fault, moment magnitude, seismic

moment, outer core, geodynamo, geoid, Airy and Pratt isostasy, flexure, hotspot. ### EA.O.A3 Deep time Situation. The record orders and ages events across 4.5 billion years. Complication. v1 said all time-scale boundaries are reference sections, misattributed Steno's rules and filed uniformitarianism twice. Question. Which claims about the sequence and age of Earth events does EA own? Answer. EA owns relative order, correlation, numeric age, the time-scale convention and the occurrence of life in the record. The decay law is PH. Key line (inductive; plural noun: time claims; dimension: how the

time is established; order: relative before numeric before convention). Members (5): Relative order · Correlation · Numeric age · Time-scale convention · Record of life and climate. - EA.O.A3.1 Relative order. Steno (1669) gave superposition, original horizontality and lateral continuity. Superposition holds for undisturbed, non-overturned layered sequences. Cross-cutting relations are credited to Steno and Hutton. The principle of inclusions is Lyell's. An unconformity is evidence of missing time. - EA.O.A3.2 Correlation. Matching strata between places by fossils, lithology, magnetic polarity, stable isotopes or tephra. An index fossil is widespread, short-lived

and distinctive. A polarity reversal is a time marker, not a cause. - EA.O.A3.3 Numeric age. The decay law N = N₀e^(−λt) is owned by PH (uses PH nuclear cell). The dating claim is owned here. It holds when the system closed at a stated time, with known initial daughter and no later gain or loss. Carbon-14 serves late-Quaternary organic matter, to about 50,000 years. U–Pb and other systems serve deep time. Luminescence, dendrochronology and varves are other numeric methods. - EA.O.A3.4 Time-scale convention. The ICS chart divides eon, era,

period, epoch and age. Phanerozoic and Ediacaran boundaries are GSSPs (reference sections). Most Precambrian boundaries are GSSAs, numeric ages such as 2500 Ma for Archean–Proterozoic. Warrant W12. - EA.O.A3.5 Record of life and climate. Occurrence of organisms in strata is owned here; their biology is BI.O.A4.5. Mass extinctions are pattern claims about that record. Paleoclimate and paleoceanography as dated states, read from proxies, are owned here. Their mechanism cites EA.O.A4.3. The Anthropocene as a formal unit was rejected by the IUGS in March 2024 (stratigraphy.org/news/152). Named objects: superposition, unconformity, index

fossil, polarity chron, closure temperature, U–Pb, GSSP, GSSA, proxy record. ### EA.O.A4 Surface and fluid envelopes Situation. Land, water, air, ice and soil are arranged and circulate at and above the surface now. Complication. Atmosphere, ocean and cryosphere had no owner; Darcy's law lacked hypotheses; hydrogeology sat in two halves. Question. Which claims about the present surface and its fluid envelopes does EA own? Answer. EA owns landforms and process, water on and under land, the atmosphere–ocean–climate state and circulation, the cryosphere, and the soil body. Key line (inductive; plural

noun: surface and envelope claims; dimension: which part of the surface system the claim is about; order: solid surface outward then back to the skin). Members (5): Landforms and process · Water on and under land · Atmosphere, ocean and climate · Cryosphere · Soil. - EA.O.A4.1 Landforms and process. Geomorphology: landforms as products of rock, climate and time. Processes are weathering, mass wasting, fluvial, glacial, aeolian and coastal. A graded river adjusts slope and channel to its water and sediment load. The adjustment is a tendency, not a guarantee.

Uniformitarianism is a methodological premise in EA.M.H, cited here. - EA.O.A4.2 Water on and under land. Water balance for a drainage basin over a period: P = ET + Q + ΔS (precipitation, evapotranspiration, runoff, storage change). Groundwater and aquifer claims (transmissivity, storativity) are owned here. Darcy's law q = −K∇h holds for laminar flow (Reynolds number below about 1–10) in a saturated, rigid porous medium. Its owner is EN transport closure (uses EN.O.A2); CONTESTED, alternative PH continuum. The well is EN. - EA.O.A4.3 Atmosphere, ocean and climate. Climate is

the statistics of weather over a stated period, typically 30 years (WMO). Its state, circulation and change as a dated Earth claim are owned here. Controls are latitude, altitude, continentality, ocean currents and circulation. The governing laws (Navier–Stokes, radiative transfer, thermodynamics) are PH. Ocean circulation, sea level and marine biogeochemical state are owned here; marine biology is BI.O.A5. Köppen–Geiger is a classification (W12), not a mechanism. Climate change attribution claims owe W2 and W5. Atmospheric electricity and the upper atmosphere are refused to PH (space physics). - EA.O.A4.4 Cryosphere. Glaciers,

ice sheets, sea ice, permafrost and snow as surface mass. Mass balance (accumulation minus ablation) is the core claim. Glacier flow by Glen's flow law assumes power-law creep of polycrystalline ice with exponent near 3 (UNVERIFIED exponent range). Glacial landforms are EA.O.A4.1. - EA.O.A4.5 Soil. The soil body: weathered parent material plus organic matter, organised in horizons. Pedology owns the profile here. Soil mechanics (effective stress, Mohr–Coulomb) is EN. Soil chemistry is CH. Soil biota are BI.O.A5.3. Named objects: drainage basin, base level, water balance, aquifer, Darcy's law, climate normal,

thermohaline circulation, mass balance, permafrost, soil horizon, Köppen–Geiger class. ### EA.O.A5 Human spatial organization Situation. People locate, move, and make places and regions under constraint. Complication. v1 filed distance decay three ways, defined vulnerability wrongly, gave hazard and risk no cell, and had no home for coupled human–natural systems. Question. Which claims about the spatial organisation of people does EA own? Answer. EA owns location and interaction, region and place, economic and urban pattern, political space, and nature–society with risk. Key line (inductive; plural noun: spatial-organisation claims; dimension: what organises

the pattern; order: distance, then meaning, then market, then authority, then nature). Members (5): Location and interaction · Region and place · Economic and urban pattern · Political space · Nature–society and risk. - EA.O.A5.1 Location and interaction. Site and situation; absolute and relative location. Distance decay is the claim that interaction falls with distance, modified by origin and destination size. It is owned here. Gravity-model estimation is EA.M.5. In trade, the gravity equation has structural derivations (Anderson 1979; Anderson and van Wincoop 2003); that derivation is EC. In migration,

gravity models are mostly reduced-form. CONTESTED for migration. - EA.O.A5.2 Region and place. A region is a delimited area of stated similarity (formal), flow (functional) or perception (perceptual). Place is a location invested with meaning; its warrant is W8. Area studies as a catalog of regions is refused (sector, not a cell). - EA.O.A5.3 Economic and urban pattern. Where production and exchange happen. Central place theory predicts a hexagonal hierarchy on an isotropic plain with uniform population and transport, and rational, nearest-centre consumers. The spatial pattern is owned here. Bid-rent

as allocation is EC. Urban models (concentric, sector, multiple nuclei) are ideal types. - EA.O.A5.4 Political space. Territory and boundary as spatial claims. A boundary is a claim enforced, not a natural line. The authority behind it is PO. Its legal validity is LA. - EA.O.A5.5 Nature–society and risk. Coupled human–natural systems: pressure, state, impact and response, under a stated boundary. This absorbs environmental science claims (Grok "EV"). Risk = hazard × exposure × vulnerability (IPCC AR6 WGII glossary). Vulnerability is the propensity to be adversely affected: sensitivity plus lack

of capacity to cope and adapt. Exposure is a separate factor. The hazard cites EA.O.A2 or A4. Policy is PO; price is EC; duty is LA. Population counts are MS.O.A5. Named objects: site, situation, distance decay, formal region, place, central place, bid-rent pattern, boundary, territory, hazard, exposure, vulnerability, risk. Pattison (1964) mapping, corrected. Spatial tradition → A5.1 and the map pattern of A4. Earth-science tradition → A1–A4. Man–land tradition → A5.5. Area-studies tradition → refused as a catalog of regions.

Face O — Objects ### MD.O.A1 Disorders **SCQA.** Medicine first names what is wrong. Names come from classification rules (conventions), but the entities they name are meant to be real. the person. The concept itself is debated in PL; MD uses a working definition. - MD.O.A1.1.1 Immune disorders: autoimmunity, immunodeficiency, allergy. Normal immune function is BI. - MD.O.A1.1.2 Neoplasms: the clinical entity is here; the cell biology is BI. - **MD.O.A1.2 Classification.** ICD-11 (in effect from 1 January 2022) and DSM-5-TR (2022). (CONTESTED). - MD.O.A1.3.1 Categorical against dimensional models (RDoC, HiTOP) as competing classification programmes. - **MD.O.A1.4 Syndromes and multimorbidity.** Co-occurring conditions; frailty. ### MD.O.A2 Causes and mechanisms **SCQA.** Why does the disorder occur? and drugs **SCQA.** What changes the course of a disorder? Drugs, procedures and therapies are tested in trials, approved by regulators and monitored after approval. The molecule is CH. - MD.O.A4.1.1 First-order elimination: half-life t½ = ln 2 / k, for linear kinetics. - MD.O.A4.1.2 Therapeutic index as the ratio of toxic to effective dose. -

MD.O.A4.1.3 Pharmacogenomics: genotype-dependent drug response. - **MD.O.A4.2 Surgery and procedures.** - **MD.O.A4.3 Psychological and rehabilitative therapy.** Cognitive behavioural therapy; physiotherapy. The mental mechanism is MS. - **MD.O.A4.4 Drug safety.** Adverse effects; pharmacovigilance after approval. - MD.O.A4.4.1 Residues of veterinary drugs in human food: the safety limit is MD; the animal treatment is AG. - **MD.O.A4.5 Drug development and regulation.** Trial phases I–IV; approval by bodies such as Medsafe (NZ), the FDA and EMA. are prevented rather than treated. Population claims rest on surveillance and study design. is LA; policy is PO. - **MD.O.A5.5 Global and Māori health.** Health inequities by population. Under the two-mode rule, the tradition-internal side of rongoā and hauora is IK. Its clinical efficacy for a named condition is MD under W3.

- EN.O.A1.2.5 Kirchhoff–Love plate and Mindlin–Reissner plate. ## 2. Governing thought Computer science is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Its objects divide into five properties of a computation: correctness, cost, coordination, learning, and protection. ## 3. Key line Dimension: **the property asserted of a computation.** Order: structural, from the single program outward to many agents and adversaries. 1. Correctness 2. Cost 3. Coordination 4. Learning 5. Protection ## 4. Face O — Objects ### CS.O.A1 Correctness **SCQA.** A computation is first judged by whether it does what it is specified

to do. Specifications, semantics and proof tools exist, but most software is never proved. What can be claimed about correctness, and how? Key line: semantics, specification and verification, types, testing. - CS.O.A1.1 Semantics of languages — operational, denotational and axiomatic semantics. Lambda calculus and Turing machines are equivalent in power (the theorem is MA.O.A1). - CS.O.A1.2 Specification and verification — Hoare logic proves partial correctness; total correctness also needs termination. Model checking decides temporal properties of finite-state models. - CS.O.A1.3 Types — well-typed programs do not go wrong (progress and

preservation), for languages whose type system is proved sound. - CS.O.A1.4 Testing — testing can show the presence of bugs, never their absence (Dijkstra), for any input space too large to exhaust. - CS.O.A1.5 Limits of correctness — Rice's theorem: every non-trivial semantic property of programs is undecidable, for Turing-complete languages. Uses MA.O.A1. ### CS.O.A2 Cost **SCQA.** A correct computation may still be too slow, too large or too costly in energy. Which costs can be bounded, and by what? Key line: algorithms, data structures, complexity, machines. - CS.O.A2.1 Algorithms

— each algorithm has a stated cost on a stated model. Comparison sorting needs Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case (a decision-tree lower bound, uses MA.B.C3). - CS.O.A2.2 Data structures — amortised costs, e.g. union–find with path compression and union by rank runs in O(α(n)) per operation. - CS.O.A2.3 Complexity classes — P, NP, PSPACE. Whether P = NP is OPEN and owned by MA.B.C3; CS uses it. - CS.O.A2.4 Machines and architecture — memory hierarchy, pipelines, parallel speed-up. Amdahl's law bounds speed-up by 1/((1−p) + p/s) for

a fixed workload whose fraction p is parallelisable by a factor s. - CS.O.A2.5 Physical limits of hardware — Moore's law is an empirical trend, now slowing; it is not a law. Transistor physics is PH. ### CS.O.A3 Coordination **SCQA.** Many computations run at once, share state and communicate over unreliable links. What can and cannot be coordinated? Key line: concurrency, distributed agreement, networks, data systems. - CS.O.A3.1 Concurrency — races, deadlock, linearisability. - CS.O.A3.2 Distributed agreement — FLP (Fischer, Lynch and Paterson, 1985): no deterministic protocol guarantees consensus in

an asynchronous system if even one process may crash. This is a proved theorem, not an open problem. Byzantine agreement needs n ≥ 3f + 1 processes to tolerate f faulty ones, with synchronous oral messages and no signatures. - CS.O.A3.3 Consistency under partition — CAP (Gilbert and Lynch, 2002 proof): during a network partition, a system cannot provide both linearisable consistency and availability. - CS.O.A3.4 Networks — protocols, routing, congestion control. - CS.O.A3.5 Data systems — databases, transactions (ACID), query optimisation. Information retrieval as a claim about records is

IS. ### CS.O.A4 Learning **SCQA.** Some computations improve from data instead of from a programmer's rules. What can such systems learn, and how well? Key line: learning theory, models and training, reasoning and planning, perception and language. - CS.O.A4.1 Learning theory — a binary concept class is PAC-learnable if and only if its VC dimension is finite (uses MA.O.A5). No-free-lunch: averaged uniformly over all objective functions, every optimiser performs equally. - CS.O.A4.2 Models and training — neural networks; universal approximation holds for one-hidden-layer networks with a non-polynomial activation, approximating continuous

functions on compact sets to any accuracy. It says nothing about learnability. Empirical scaling laws are W4 claims within stated ranges. - CS.O.A4.3 Reasoning and planning — search, logic programming, planning. Many planning problems are PSPACE-complete (uses MA.B.C3). - CS.O.A4.4 Perception and language processing — vision, speech, NLP. Claims about language itself are LN. - CS.O.A4.5 Alignment and evaluation of AI systems — whether a trained system pursues its intended objective. Methods are immature; much is OPEN. ### CS.O.A5 Protection **SCQA.** Computations run among adversaries. What can be protected, from

whom, and on what assumptions? Key line: cryptography in use, security of systems, privacy. - CS.O.A5.1 Cryptography in use — protocols are secure relative to stated hardness assumptions (e.g. factoring). Security proofs are MA; the deployed protocol is CS. - CS.O.A5.2 Systems security — access control, memory safety, attack surfaces. - CS.O.A5.3 Privacy — differential privacy bounds how much one record changes an output distribution, by a stated ε. - CS.O.A5.4 Quantum threats — Shor's algorithm factors in polynomial time on a fault-tolerant quantum computer. Uses MA.B.C3 and PH.O.A2.

Choice theory is precise, but people often depart from its axioms. What is claimed about how agents choose? Key line: preferences, choice under risk, behavioural departures, intertemporal choice. - EC.O.A1.1 Preferences and demand — complete, transitive and

continuous preferences have a utility representation (Debreu; proof uses MA). Demand theory follows, with the Slutsky decomposition. - EC.O.A1.2 Choice under risk — expected utility follows from the von Neumann–Morgenstern axioms (completeness, transitivity, continuity, independence). - EC.O.A1.3 Behavioural departures — the Allais paradox violates independence; prospect theory fits loss aversion. Key line: competitive equilibrium, market power, information, factor markets. - EC.O.A2.1 Competitive equilibrium — a general equilibrium exists given continuous, convex, locally non-satiated preferences, convex production, and endowments in the interior (Arrow–Debreu; proof MA). - EC.O.A2.2 Market power — monopoly, oligopoly, entry. The equilibrium of the Cournot or Bertrand game is MA. Which game the firms are in is ST. The resulting prices and quantities are EC. - EC.O.A2.3 Information — adverse selection (Akerlof), moral hazard, signalling. A market can unravel when quality is hidden and sellers

of game ST. ### EC.O.A4 The aggregate economy **SCQA.** Output, prices and employment move together across an economy. What determines them? Key line: growth, fluctuations, money and inflation, open economies. - EC.O.A4.1 Growth — the Solow model: with diminishing returns to capital and constant returns to scale, output per worker converges to a steady state, and long-run growth needs technical change. - EC.O.A4.2 Fluctuations — business cycles; unemployment. The Phillips curve is an empirical relation that proved unstable once expectations adjusted. - EC.O.A4.3 Money and inflation — the quantity equation

Key line: welfare theorems, market failure, public finance, social choice. - EC.O.A5.1 First welfare theorem — with complete markets, price-taking agents, locally non-satiated preferences and no externalities, every competitive equilibrium is Pareto efficient. Theorem MA; use EC. - EC.O.A5.3 Market failure — externalities,

public goods, common pool resources. Pigouvian taxes correct an externality when its marginal damage is known. - EC.O.A5.4 Public finance — taxes and spending. A VAT is levied on value added at each stage, with credit for tax paid on inputs. A retail sales tax is levied once, on the final sale. and non-dictatorship together. Theorem MA; the meaning for collective choice is EC; the normative argument is PL.
